precepts.label: Zechariah 2:6-7
precepts.why:
Jacob called his sons to tell them “that which shall befall you in the last days,” and of Judah he said, “thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies.” That says two things: Judah will be fighting his enemy, and Judah will be living in close proximity to his enemy, who today is Esau, Edom. Zechariah 2 is the scripture that proves Judah will be living with that enemy.

“Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north, saith the Lord: for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven, saith the Lord.” Then: “Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” Zion is the city of Judah. The daughter of Babylon, as Psalms 137 shows, is Edom, the Caucasian race. So Zion is dwelling with the daughter of Babylon: Judah living in the land of the north, in the house of his enemy.

That is the picture of Genesis 49:8. Judah’s hand in the neck of his enemies is Judah living with him and contending with him. In the 1960s and 70s there was the Black Panthers, Martin Luther King, Malcolm X, and many movements where Judah rose up and fought the so-called white man. “he stooped down, he couched as a lion,” and at one point it looked like he was about to strike.

But the lion lay back down: “as an old lion; who shall rouse him up?” Christ is the one who will rouse him up. Until then the word to Zion is to come forth and deliver himself from the daughter of Babylon he dwells with.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 32:26
precepts.why:
“And they shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder, and upon thy seed for ever.” Why a sign? When you see a McDonald's sign, it lets you know a McDonald's is there. The curses have to be upon us for a sign because we would be cut off from our heritage, and in the future Judah will need to identify who Israel is. How do you identify the Israelites today? By the curses.

Deuteronomy 32:26 shows why: “I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men”. We were scattered into corners in slavery, and the remembrance of who we are, our nationality, all of it, has ceased from among men. We did not just forget because time went on. We forgot because the nations made war with us and took crafty counsel: make sure those slaves cannot read and write. They destroyed us as a people and took our nationality. Ask a Chinese man today who the Israelites are, and he points at the fake people in the land, the synagogue of Satan.

Yet go to Africa today and you will see millions of people professing that they are the people of God, the Israelites, though you will not see it on the news. Just in Nigeria there is a large Israelite community of millions. Over generations of misinterpretation and mixing customs with the Hamitic tribes they do not keep the laws the way they are supposed to, but they always knew they were Israel.

So God did it real nice. Esau would take our nationality from us, but the curses would follow us and our seed, so that no matter where we are scattered, in Africa, America, South America, China, Iran, the islands, when we read the Bible we say: wait, this is talking about my people.

precepts.label: Zechariah 12:7
precepts.why:
“Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him unto his people”. There is Judah in Africa too, but this is speaking of Judah on this side of the earth, in the Western Hemisphere, specifically in the United States of America. Judah in North America is under Esau, who controls the world right now, and with an American passport you can go anywhere in the world. A Jamaican, Haitian or Nigerian passport cannot take you everywhere. That is why we tell you brothers: get your passport.

“The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first”. God is going to raise up the tribe of Judah first, Judah in America. Then, when it says bring him unto his people, it means Judah will know where God's people are and will go find them. Wherever our people are in Africa, in Japan, in Iran, in India, scattered throughout the four corners of the earth, Judah will be able to identify them, find them, and teach them what God commanded of them.

That is why Genesis 49 speaks mainly of Israel on this side of the world: Judah needed to know who they were first. And it is already happening. The bishops and brothers that travel went into the history of the people, and they found Judah among the Igbo of Nigeria and the tribes scattered across Africa, India and the islands, now written on the revised twelve tribe chart. When people ask how we know, it is because the Lord showed us; the spirit guided us. That is “be thou an help to him from his enemies”: God is a help to Judah, making us find things so we are not guessing, and the chart will keep being updated as the Lord reveals more.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 11:18
precepts.why:
The Song of Solomon is a metaphor: the whole book represents the Lord's relationship with his chosen people, Israel. So what did Solomon mean, in his righteousness, when he said “Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm”? The heart is the mind. What is set as a seal upon our mind and upon our arm? Is it the six-point hexagram? Heck no. Here is what he was referring to.

“Therefore shall ye lay up these my words in your heart and in your soul”. These my words are the laws of God, laid up in your heart, meaning your mind. “and bind them for a sign upon your hand, that they may be as frontlets between your eyes.” In ancient times Israel would write the laws on leather and wrap them around their arms. Those were the frontlets, and the frontlets between your eyes are on your forehead.

So go back to the Song: “Set me as a seal upon thine heart”, that's the mind; “as a seal upon thine arm”. The seal is the law, the laws of God, the words of God, bound on the arm and laid up in the mind. People who will not be proven wrong search for scriptures that use the word shield or seal and try to make them say it is the Star of David, forcing a square peg into a circle. That is a complete lie; the seal is the law.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 10:21-23
precepts.why:
Ezra lays out everything Israel lost: “our sanctuary is laid waste, our altar broken down, our temple destroyed; Our psaltery is laid on the ground”. The psaltery is the music. “our song is put to silence, our rejoicing is at an end, the light of our candlestick is put out”, the menorah is put out. “the ark of our covenant is spoiled, our holy things are defiled, and the name that is called upon us is almost profaned”, the name Israel.

It goes on: “our children are put to shame, our priests are burnt, our Levites are gone into captivity, our virgins are defiled, and our wives ravished”, our wives were raped; “our righteous men carried away, our little ones destroyed, our young men are brought in bondage, and our strong men are become weak”.

Then: “And, which is the greatest of all, the seal of Sion hath now lost her honour; for she is delivered into the hands of them that hate us.” What is the seal of Zion? Is that talking about the six-point hexagram, the star of Remphan, the star of Moloch? No. Isaiah shows what the seal of Zion is: the law.

So the seal Solomon asked to be set upon the heart and the arm is the same seal of Zion Ezra mourned: the law of God. The greatest of all Israel's losses was not a symbol but the honour of the law, delivered into the hands of them that hate us.

precepts.label: Isaiah 8:16
precepts.why:
Ezra said “the seal of Sion hath now lost her honour”. Here is what the seal of Zion is: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” Seal the law among my disciples. The law is the seal. The law is the seal.

That is what Solomon meant by “Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm”: the law of God set on the mind and bound on the arm, as Deuteronomy said to bind the words for a sign upon the hand. It is not the six-pointed star.

And it is the same seal the servants of God are sealed with in Revelation. So what is the seal we have to be sealed with? The law. The law. The law. There is nothing else to be said about it; if you keep pushing that star, that is your own vain opinion. Brothers and sisters, come on one accord and stop following the so-called white man and his lies.

precepts.label: Revelation 7:3-4
precepts.why:
“And I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” Then jump up to verse 3: “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.”

What is the seal talking about? Go right back to Isaiah 8:16: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” The servants of God are sealed in their foreheads with the law, the same place Deuteronomy said the words of God would be “as frontlets between your eyes”, in the mind. Some are still saying the star of Moloch, the star of David; that is simple.

So the seal of Song of Solomon 8:6, set upon the heart and upon the arm, is the seal of the servants of God in Revelation: the law, laid up in the mind of the tribes of the children of Israel.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 30:11
precepts.why:
Isaiah says, “As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them.” These same kids become the neighborhood oppressors, running around with Glocks and taped-up mags and all that foolishness, and there is no man anywhere in the picture: no man with authority, no dignity, no order, no structure. Ecclesiasticus gives the charge that was missing: “Give him no liberty in his youth, and wink not at his follies.”

You have to hold those children in. You have to take that by the reins, because you are the one who is going to form their thoughts, their shape and their identity. Don’t give them liberty in their youth, and don’t wink at their follies.

Look at what happens when that is not done. They wanted to kill Julio Foolio over a rap battle: young, dumb, stupid people, wise to do evil. They used a girl’s phone to track him, bought AR-15 type weapons with brass catchers so the shells would not be left at the scene, and shot up his birthday party at a hotel. They thought they got away, but the police got every camera, the house cameras, the phone records, the tag readers and the Flock cameras, and the investigators took their time and put the pieces together. Lock, seal, smack, boom, you’re going down. Your ass is in jail and your mind is still a child. When the enticement wears off, reality seeps back in, and it usually comes with the arrest.

We have children in our nation too, some disrespectful to their parents, some who won’t listen. You don’t know what your parents are trying to save you from, and once you learn it, it may be too late to turn around. That behavior is not normal, not for our people, the royalty, and not period. And the eighth head knows this. They don’t care if it touches some of theirs; that is collateral damage. Their elite make sure their own children get the lessons they need to not fall into it. We are the only ones who eat this stuff up.

precepts.label: Daniel 12:6-7
precepts.why:
Hosea says the children of Israel “shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod”. Daniel 12 gives the time frame for it. “How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?” The wonders are our people being destroyed, enslaved and colonized, being without a king, without a prince, without an ephod.

“it shall be for a time, times, and an half”. A time is a hundred years; times is two hundred, three hundred in all; and an half makes 350 years. “and when he shall have accomplished to scatter the power of the holy people, all these things shall be finished.” Within those 350 years we were totally destroyed. All that power was gone from us; we forgot who we are, and we even forgot our nationality.

When we fled Jerusalem in 70 AD, was our power destroyed? Our country was destroyed, but we went to Africa and built cities there, and the ten tribes were set up on this side of the world doing their thing too. We still had governments, we still had kings over us, and we still knew we were the children of Israel. It was within the slave trade and colonization that the power of the holy people was scattered.

That is the many days without a king: without political sovereignty, when Europe colonized Ghana, Nigeria, Angola, Senegal, Papua New Guinea and the Congo, and when the transatlantic slave trade took us. It is without an image: our minds destroyed until the sisters in Africa bleach their skin and put on weaves, because worshipping the God of your oppressor destroys the way you look at yourself. The same curses fell on our people all over Africa, like the Mau Mau in Kenya, tortured in British camps and paid less than 4,000 pounds each. That is why I don't want no damn reparations.

precepts.label: Daniel 12:11
precepts.why:
Daniel 12 gives the time frame for when our people would be without a king, without an image, and without a sacrifice, as Hosea 3:4 says. Verse 11 reads: “And from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days.”

The daily sacrifice taken away is Hosea's “without a sacrifice”. Without the sacrifice, the image and the ephod, all our religious infrastructure and spiritual guidance was stripped away, and there was no priest to guide us and tell us what God needs us to do. The white man came in, whipped us, taught us white Jesus and his lies, and forced it down our throats in Africa. After he brought the slaves over here, he went to Africa and destroyed them there, until the people in Africa don't even know that we in the Caribbean and America are the same people.

So from the taking away of the sacrifice, the days are counted, and the question Daniel asked, “How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?”, is answered with a set time. That goes back to the yoke of iron upon thy neck until thou have been destroyed: it did not just happen to us over here, it happened to our people in Africa, and the scattering of the holy people runs its appointed course.

precepts.label: Revelation 13:10
precepts.why:
Obadiah says, “as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head.” What the nations did to us shall be done to them. That is reap what you sow. Revelation says the same: “He that leadeth into captivity shall go into captivity: he that killeth with the sword must be killed with the sword. Here is the patience and the faith of the saints.”

As they put their captivity and their evil upon the Lord's people on his holy mountain, even though we deserved it, “so shall all the heathen drink continually”. They shall drink the captivity, the slavery; they are going to get all of it. The white man and the nations that did this evil to us will not go unpunished, and the terror and evil they did to us is going to happen to them by the hands of his people, Israel.

The saints are the ones who get that opportunity, like it says in Psalms 149: this honour have all his saints. It is going to be a beautiful thing when we get that revenge. “And they shall be as though they had not been”: as though they were never a nation, the same way we are acting like we were never a nation of people.

But it happens by the hands of those that keep his commandments. That does not let our wicked children off the hook. Because they will have already witnessed how Christ dealt with the rebellious. Christ said it: “But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me.”

Everybody that is against what Christ said is an enemy of Christ, and that includes our people. You fathers and mothers try to rule over your children to keep them from going astray, and they say, I'm not having that; I'm doing my own thing; the hell with what you got to say, mama; the hell with that Bible. They refuse the correction of their fathers and mothers ruling over them, and they would not that Christ and his law should reign over them.

Honour means moral integrity, honesty and a strong code of conduct, a high respect, toward your father and your mother. “And, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death”: that is the judgment for not honouring them.

Sirach gives the measure of it: “Honour thy father with thy whole heart”. The root word for integrity is integer, meaning whole. Honour them with your whole heart. “And forget not the sorrows of thy mother”: the troubles she went through, carrying you for nine months and giving birth to you.

The young man in the courtroom is suffering as a murderer, literally. He cannot say the Lord is going to repay them for what they are doing to him; the reason he is being judged is that he broke the laws of the Most High. He broke down crying because he is a wankster, not a gangster. Where are the homies and the shoot-em-up videos now? When you get locked up, nobody cares about your black ass once you are in jail. Esau is the devil for a reason; he lets the little negro run around with a gun killing his own people, and then he busts him, and he becomes property of the state, sweat equity for the prison system.

That is where many of our sons and daughters are going when they refuse to listen to their parents: if not jail, a pregnancy, a disease, a marriage riddled with alcohol abuse and domestic violence. That is why God gave children parents. We were not afraid of the power before; we broke the commandments, so the Lord put this beast over us, and when you mess up with him he has no pity. As they say in the islands, those who don’t hear will feel. Suffer, if you must, as a follower of Christ, never as an evildoer.

precepts.label: Matthew 5:10
precepts.why:
“For rulers are not a terror to good works”. The powers that be are not a terror to those of us that keep the commandments of God. Even though we are persecuted for it, it is not a terror to us, because we know what it is about. We are in captivity, but we are doing what God said to do, and they are going to have to answer to the Father for their mistreatment of us.

That is because of this promise: “Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness’ sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.” If I am going to get locked up for doing what is right, I will suffer for that.

Being persecuted for righteousness’ sake deals with a whole different kind of mentality. All the words they say to me will not mean anything, because I am suffering for a worthy cause, and I know that after that, mine is the kingdom of heaven. You can go through that trial and say, the Lord is going to receive me because I did what was right.

That is a totally different mentality than going in as a murderer. Suffering as a murderer, you are still going to get jacked up at the end; you are not getting the kingdom. So do that which is good, and if the rulers persecute you for it, the kingdom of heaven is yours.

precepts.label: Ephesians 6:1-4
precepts.why:
“Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. Honour thy father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;) That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth.” “And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.”

These scriptures are put together with “Put on the whole armour of God” for a reason. If you do half of these things, you are not putting on the whole armour of God; you are putting on pieces. It begins at home. Husbands in order, wives in order; if they are not in order, you can't expect the children to be in order.

Children learn how to obey the Lord by the behavior of their parents, and in turn they are putting on the whole armour of God. The father brings them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord, and that is how a family stands against the wiles of the devil.

precepts.label: Ephesians 5:22-23
precepts.why:
“Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body.”

The whole armour of God is not put on in pieces. If we want to strengthen our families: one, the husband in order; the wife in order; and the children will learn how to obey the Lord by your behavior. The husband is the head as Christ is the head, and the wife submits as unto the Lord.

If the husband and wife are not in order, you can't expect the children to be in order. So the order of the house, the husband as head and the wife submitting, is part of the armour that lets the family “stand against the wiles of the devil.”

precepts.label: Ephesians 5:15-16
precepts.why:
“See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.”

This is another piece of the whole armour. If you are not redeeming the time because the days are evil, you are not going to teach your children to learn how to fear God. Walking circumspectly, not as fools but as wise, is how a parent sets the example the children follow.

The days are evil: the social media zaps our young out, and Esau sets it up so they can be taken for sweat equity. Redeeming the time means using it for the Lord and for teaching the house, so the family can put on the whole armour of God and “stand against the wiles of the devil.”

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 6:7
precepts.why:
“And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children”. Teach them what? The laws of God. “and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.”

It is a routine of the word. It's repetition: sitting in the house, walking by the way, lying down, rising up. Children are not mature enough to make that cognitive decision on their own; the parent has to put the law in them diligently, over and over.

That is how the children put on the whole armour of God. The husband in order, the wife in order, the time redeemed, and the laws taught diligently at every part of the day, so the house can “stand against the wiles of the devil.”

precepts.label: Ephesians 5:19
precepts.why:
“Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord”.

Over and over you sing these songs, you read these words. It's repetition, the same routine of the word Moses commanded when he said to teach the laws diligently in the house, by the way, lying down and rising up. It is there to mold the children's minds concerning the laws of God.

The world molds them with its music and its social media; the psalms, hymns and spiritual songs mold them with the law. That repetition in the house is part of putting on the whole armour of God, so they can “stand against the wiles of the devil.”

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 6:12
precepts.why:
“Then beware lest thou forget the Lord, which brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage.”

That's why you do it: why you teach the laws diligently to the children, talk of them in the house and by the way, and sing the psalms and spiritual songs over and over. The repetition keeps the house from forgetting the Lord who brought us out of the house of bondage.

Now if you forget the Lord, guess what? You're going to be tempted. Forgetting the Lord leaves the armour off, and the wiles of the devil find a way in. Remembering him is how the family puts on the whole armour of God and stands.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 6:16-17
precepts.why:
“Ye shall not tempt the Lord your God, as ye tempted him in Massah. Ye shall diligently keep the commandments of the Lord your God, and his testimonies, and his statutes, which he hath commanded thee.”

Well, how don't you tempt him? Teach them diligently. Husband in order, wife in order, redeeming the time. Diligently keeping the commandments, testimonies and statutes: that's how you do it, by instructing them.

So all these scriptures go together. Do half of them and you have only pieces of the armour. Do them all, in the house, with the children, and the family has put on the whole armour of God, “that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.”

“And there appeared a great wonder in heaven; a woman clothed with the sun.” Who is this woman? Jeremiah says, “I have likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman.” The Lord has likened his people to a comely, delicate woman.

So that is the woman Revelation 12 is talking about: the twelve tribes of Israel. Keep that in mind through the whole chapter. “upon her head a crown of twelve stars”: the twelve stars are the twelve tribes, which is why she is called that way.

When “she being with child cried, travailing in birth, and pained to be delivered”, it is the nation of Israel travailing to bring forth Christ, to save us from the hand of the Romans who had taken the kingdom of Israel by force. Pained to be delivered means we were persecuted. Everything that happens to the woman in this chapter is the history of our people.

precepts.label: Psalms 147:19-20
precepts.why:

The psalm says so: “He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel. He hath not dealt so with any nation: and as for his judgments, they have not known them.”

God gave his word, his statutes and his judgments to Jacob and to Israel, and he has not dealt so with any other nation. That is why the woman is clothed with that light and no one else is. The woman crowned with twelve stars and clothed with the sun and moon is the nation that received the law: the twelve tribes of Israel.

precepts.label: Matthew 2:13
precepts.why:
“she being with child cried, travailing in birth, and pained to be delivered.” Pained to be delivered means we were persecuted. Matthew shows the persecution. Herod sent out an edict to look for Christ to kill him, and they were killing our babies from two years old and under. These bastards were murdering our children like they seek to do today. Bastards, because the Most High said they are not his children: if you be without chastisement, then are ye bastards, because a bastard has no father.

“behold, the angel of the Lord appeareth to Joseph in a dream, saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be thou there until I bring thee word: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.”

If Jesus was a white boy, how could you hide him in Egypt, a black country? He would have stood out like a sore thumb. He was able to hide among black people because Jesus is black, and his mother and father are black. They have been lying on this Bible all along.

That is the persecution Revelation 12 is talking about: the dragon “stood before the woman which was ready to be delivered, for to devour her child as soon as it was born.” Herod was an Idumean, and Idumea is a word for Edom; that is in the history books. So the scripture names the dragon. The people running this system are not your friends; they want to see us destroyed and in slavery.

precepts.label: Matthew 11:11-12
precepts.why:
“And there appeared another wonder in heaven”: in our heaven. Christ explains why it is said that way. “Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist: notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.” Nobody was greater than John the Baptist except Christ; he was the forerunner to Christ. So the subject matter at this time is the kingdom of heaven.

“And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.” What is the kingdom of heaven? The Israelites, the twelve tribes of Israel. The kingdom of heaven where the Most High is suffered no violence. The violence was happening to us, in our kingdom.

precepts.label: Luke 21:20-24
precepts.why:

The third part is mainly Judah, Benjamin and Levi, with stragglers of the other tribes, like Anna of the tribe of Aser, still in Jerusalem; the bulk of the tribes had already gone under Cyrus. This is going into 70 AD, and Luke tells it.

“And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.” The Roman armies. It was prophesied that Jerusalem would be destroyed. “Then let them which are in Judea flee to the mountains”: our people fled into Egypt, into Africa, the same place Joseph took Jesus and his mother. Windsor's book Babylon to Timbuktu records that the slave markets were full of black Jewish slaves. “and let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto”: the other tribes were already gone, the twelve tribes scattered abroad.

“and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.” The land has white people on it calling themselves us; the Lord calls them the Gentiles. When their time is up, Psalms 149 is where they are going.

precepts.label: Hosea 1:10-11
precepts.why:
“the woman fled into the wilderness, where she hath a place prepared of God.” The wilderness is Africa, where we fled out of Jerusalem. After the wilderness we came to a place, and Hosea tells what that place is: “it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.”

This is where they destroyed our nationality, in the Americas. The place where it was said, you are not the Israelites. They called us out of our name; they called us undocumented workers. And when we pick up the Bible to gain our nationality back, they label it a hate crime, because they propagated a set of people and said these are the Jews. That is why Psalms 83 says they have consulted that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.

“there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” That is what is happening to you, brothers and sisters, right here in Babylon the Great, in the place prepared for the woman. It means they cannot stop this gospel.

“Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head”: that one head is Christ. “and they shall come up out of the land”: that is when we go home.

“where also our Lord was crucified.” Christ was not physically crucified here, but they gave us Christianity and destroyed the minds of our people. The dead bodies are mentally and spiritually dead: dead to who we are, because they said you are not the children of Israel.

“And they of the people and kindreds and tongues and nations shall see their dead bodies three days and an half, and shall not suffer their dead bodies to be put in graves.” Three days and a half is 350 years, and we are not put in graves because we are not physically dead. “And they that dwell upon the earth shall rejoice over them, and make merry, and shall send gifts one to another”: the nations are rejoicing and celebrating over our destruction, “because these two prophets tormented them that dwelt on the earth.” They know our history and remember the power we once ruled with.

precepts.label: 1 Chronicles 12:32
precepts.why:
“For the most High then shewed signs for them, and held still the flood, till they were passed over.” The tribes that left the heathen went into the Euphrates “by the narrow places of the river” and down into the ocean, and the Most High was with them. He showed them signs, and there were men among them able to read those signs.

“And of the children of Issachar, which were men that had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do; the heads of them were two hundred; and all their brethren were at their commandment.” Issachar could read the stars. That is how they were the navigators: they had understanding of the times, they knew what Israel ought to do, and so they were able to lead the ships as the tribes came over. They knew how to navigate the waters.

They understood the winds and the currents, the Atlantic drift routes from Africa to America. Solomon understood all of this too, with the navy he had going out; the same ports Solomon’s navy knew were the stops along the route, because “through that country there was a great way to go, namely, of a year and a half”. African boatmen from Lake Chad later built a papyrus boat on the pattern of the ancient Egyptians and sailed it from North Africa as far as Barbados, proving such a drift journey on the Africa-to-America currents could be done, because the currents were understood.

So the ten tribes did not wander blindly into “a further country, where never mankind dwelt”. The Most High showed signs, Issachar read them, and the ships came across into the region called Arsareth, the land Columbus identified with America. “Then dwelt they there until the latter time”, and that is why we are here in the latter times.

precepts.label: Ezra 1:3-4
precepts.why:
Between verse 40 and verse 41 of 2 Esdras 13 there is a whole lot of history. Verse 40 is Assyria: “whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive”, before Babylon and before the Persians. Then Babylon took down Assyria and took her captives, and moved down and took Judah. Then the Persians came in. None of that is mentioned in the two verses; it jumps from Assyria to Persia, under Cyrus. So when verse 41 says “But they took this counsel among themselves”, what is the counsel? Ezra shows it.

“Who is there among you of all his people? his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of the Lord God of Israel, (he is the God,) which is in Jerusalem.” It is Cyrus speaking: the proclamation between the Most High and him, allowing Israel to go back and build in exchange for being able to take down Babylon.

“And whosoever remaineth in any place where he sojourneth, let the men of his place help him with silver, and with gold, and with goods, and with beasts, beside the freewill offering for the house of God that is in Jerusalem.” That was what was charged to Israel to go and do.

But the counsel the tribes took among themselves was different: “that they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go forth into a further country, where never mankind dwelt”. The bulk of them said, we are not staying; we are not going back to build in Jerusalem; we are going to a further country. Ezra and Nehemiah are the first two books of Ezra, and 1 Esdras and 2 Esdras are the third and fourth, and together they detail this history.

precepts.label: 1 Kings 9:26-28
precepts.why:
“For through that country there was a great way to go, namely, of a year and a half”. If it took us a year and a half to get from one area to another, don’t you think we were making stops? Maritime means things connected with the sea, oceans and navigation: shipping, commerce, naval operations. We were running those ports, and even where it was not us particularly, we had understanding with the nations we passed by. The Red Sea and the Indian Ocean connected Africa to the wider world as early as the third century BCE, with trade to Arabia, India, Persia and China.

Solomon had a navy of ships: “And king Solomon made a navy of ships in Ezion–geber, which is beside Eloth, on the shore of the Red sea, in the land of Edom. And Hiram sent in the navy his servants, shipmen that had knowledge of the sea, with the servants of Solomon.” Shipmen that had knowledge of the sea: those are the maritime men.

Ezion-geber is at the northern tip of the Red Sea’s Gulf of Aqaba, by modern-day Aqaba in Jordan and Eilat. That is very near the region where the brothers entered into the Euphrates. “And they came to Ophir, and fetched from thence gold, four hundred and twenty talents, and brought it to king Solomon.” Ophir is not far from those same areas.

So we had maritime trade going on even in Solomon’s time. It was no mystery for us to make it from where we were, out of Persia, over to the Americas, because those ports were there. That is how the journey took a year and a half, stopping at the ports, until we came into the region called Arsareth, the land Columbus identified with America.

precepts.label: Isaiah 13:12
precepts.why:
Solomon’s ships “came to Ophir, and fetched from thence gold”. Isaiah uses that same gold: “I will make a man more precious than fine gold; even a man than the golden wedge of Ophir.”

We often read this and keep going, and some will say it is the best gold, but we don’t go deeper into what the gold of Ophir is. The gold of Ophir is an exceptionally fine, pure gold, prized in the ancient world, famous as what King Solomon and King Hiram of Tyre brought in, and its exact location remains one of history’s greatest archaeological mysteries.

That is what the Most High is going to make you men: that pure fine gold. The same tribes who crossed the waters on those old maritime routes, whose record the historians call mythical, are the men the Most High will make more precious than the golden wedge of Ophir.
